subject: Biology
central_question: How do hormones from endocrine glands and other tissues coordinate metabolism, growth, reproduction and homeostasis in humans?
in_scope_units: Endocrine glands and hormones as intercellular messengers.
Pineal, thyroid, parathyroid and thymus glands.
Hormones of heart, kidney and gastrointestinal tract.

known_pitfalls.claim: The posterior pituitary synthesises oxytocin and vasopressin.
known_pitfalls.correction: They are synthesised in the hypothalamus and stored and released by the neurohypophysis.
Insulin lowers blood glucose; glucagon raises it.

known_pitfalls.claim: All hormones enter cells and act directly on DNA.
known_pitfalls.correction: Many peptide hormones use membrane receptors and second messengers; steroid and thyroid hormones commonly use intracellular receptors.

recommended_example_progression: Use NCERT Exercise 1 to distinguish exocrine glands, endocrine glands and hormones.
Use NCERT Exercise 3 to map glands to hormones.
Use NCERT Exercise 6 to classify hormones by physiological effects.
